extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of classical Euclidean geometry (readers of an Italian geometry treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules, theorems, and construction methods for plane geometry: building and comparing triangles, squares, circles, polygons, and using similar triangles to measure distances. The page gives step-by-step compass-and-straightedge constructions and accompanying explanatory remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of an equilateral triangle (triangolo equilatero)
rubrics_metrics.description: Il triangolo equilatero ebe p ciafeuna faccia ... (discussion of faces and equal angles in an equilateral triangle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that in an equilateral triangle the faces (sides) and the central angles are equal; gives construction remarks and consequences used later (e.g. comparing sides by their opposite angles and producing equal-face triangles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thales / semicircle right-angle property (semicerchio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nel semicerchio ... tutte le linee che partano dal centro al luogo del contatto cagionano afquadro (lines from the centre to the point of contact in a semicircle make a right angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a construction/principle: when a triangle is inscribed in a semicircle the angle subtended by the diameter is right; many procedures for finding catetti (legs) and right triangles rely on this fact and on drawing diameters and radii to contact points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding a cathetus (catetto) of a right triangle from given data
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to 'troua il catetto' (find the cathetus) by using semicircles, diameters, and existing sides/angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several stepwise methods: place diameters, draw lines from centers to contact points, divide segments in given proportions, and use semicircle/right-angle constructions to recover the unknown leg. The text enumerates multiple 'modi' (ways) to find the cathetus depending on which data are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a square from given segment via diagonal (quadrato via diagonale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pigliane la diagonale ... trouarai il lato: 'pigliane la... diagonale de vn quadrato trouarai il lato'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain the side of a square from a given diagonal: draw the diagonal and construct the square whose diagonal is that segment; conversely, from a square's diagonal one can recover the side. This is presented as a routine construction used repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide a circle into equal parts / construct equal 'rosette' (Dividi un cerchio ... fedi una rofetta egual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dividi un cerchio a feda al quale a oe Diametro, i o.e fedi una rofetta egual ... (divide circle into equal sectors/parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for partitioning a circle into equal arcs/areas and producing equal petal/rosette shapes; includes methods of marking diameters and equal chords, and using those equal parts in further constructions (e.g., for constructing regular polygons or equal sectors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inscribing/circumscribing polygons using diameters and side projections (poligoni inscritti e circonscritti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use diameters, perpendiculars, and known side lengths to inscribe or circumscribe squares, pentagons and other polygons: e.g., instructions for a pentagon 'pétagono' and quadrilateral constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text gives recipes: take given side lengths, project through centers, use right angles at contact points, and construct the required polygon step by step. Examples include producing a pentagon from particular triangle constructions and constructing squares adjacent to triangles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gnomonic (gnomonica) quantity computations and use of gnomon
rubrics_metrics.description: La quantità gnomonica ... la quantità gnomonica è quella al quadro piccolo ... (discussion of gnomonic quantities related to squares and their differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to compute and use the gnomon (the shape left when a smaller square is removed from a larger square) to reason about areas; shows how to decompose shapes into gnomonic parts for arithmetic and geometric proportional operations, and how to aggregate gnomonic measures ('la quantità gnomonica') for construction decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doubling and halving lengths by folding or geometric doubling (duplicare / dimezzare lunghezza)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for doubling a strip or segment by folding: 'poniamo ... duplicare la sua lunghezza' and several constructions to obtain doubled or halved segments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives practical folding/constructive instructions for obtaining double or half of a given length and for comparing resulting lengths; used when constructing longer sides from short given pieces or when replicating a side multiple times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparing which side is longer via projections and opposite angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining that a side is longer because it is opposite a greater angle: rules and operational tests for whether 'il lato ... più è largo' by comparing projections and using triangles constructed on the sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides constructions and thought experiments (projections, perpendiculars, semicircles) to compare two sides of a triangle: move or project points, form right triangles, and observe which cathetus or projection is longer, concluding which original side is greater.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute diameters and scale diameters by proportional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for computing a circle's diameter, halving/doubling diameters, and deriving diameters of inscribed/related circles by proportion and repeated doubling/halving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to obtain a circle's diameter from related circles or figures by proportional manipulations (e.g., 'la metà ...', 'Doppia ... 12 f' etc.); used across constructions where circles of various sizes are related arithmetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing polygonal parts from central lines perpendicular to tangency (center-to-contact perpendicularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a line is drawn from the centre to the contact point with another figure (e.g., contact of circle and polygon), that line is perpendicular to the tangent/side at the point of contact: 'tutte le linee che partano dal centro al luogo del contatto cagionano afquadro'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This geometric fact is used repeatedly to establish right angles, to place perpendiculars, and to justify right-triangle constructions derived from circle contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of similar triangles and sight-lines to measure heights and distances (measuring by similar triangles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a known height (person, pole, table) and sight-lines through windows or along planes to form similar right triangles, enabling computation of unknown heights/distances: 'la tua statura... triangolo rettangolo... calcuicatteoe... latuaperfona ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a practical measurement procedure: place yourself at known distances, note lines of sight across apertures, construct similar triangles and proportional segments to compute remote heights or distances using compass-and-straightedge/arithmetical proportions. The text works through examples with a table, window, and poles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations between concentric circles and counting steps/rotations (concentric-circle walking problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two circles with the same centre, one larger and one smaller, and a point walking around yields relations of encounter and counting of turns/days: e.g. 'due cerchi uno e grande e l'altro piccolo ... uno camina e circundalo tutto in 12 dì ... poi l'altro ... in 1/2 dì ... Domando in quanti giorni faranno ...' (how many times they meet/opposite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a geometric/arithmetic problem combining circular motion with counting periods and proportional distances; the text explains how to equate angular travel and compare counts of meetings by reducing to ratios of circumferences/diameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing and comparing inscribed small and large circles to determine visible and hidden portions (lucida/dura, visible/obscure parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two spheres/circles, one 'lucida' (bright) and one 'dura' (dark), and drawing diameters and parallel chords to determine exposed/hidden areas and their measures: 'una tutta lucida l'altra tutta obscura... tirarai una...' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives rules for marking diameters and corresponding parallel sections to compute the parts of circles/spheres that are visible/illuminated versus hidden; used to reason about overlapping disks and relative portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing rectangles/windows and using projections to find remote lengths (sight-lines & window method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a rectangular aperture (window) and projecting lines from eye to far points to create similar triangles whose legs yield distances: 'la tua statura... la tua persona... la larghezza della tavola... triangoli rettangoli... la linea g f...' etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed recipes: position observer and object relative to a rectangular frame, draw the sight-line to opposite corners, construct the corresponding triangles on the ground plane, and use proportionality between those triangles to calculate remote distances. Includes instructions how to adjust if the window (frame) is not perpendicular or when heights differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposing squares and quadrilaterals into smaller parts for area/construction uses (cutting squares into parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for cutting a square into smaller squares/rectangles and arranging pieces (e.g., 'taglierai per l'altro vero del quadrato gride ... il quadrato piccolo ... quantità gnomonica ...'), used to compute gnomonic measures and to assemble larger figures from smaller ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives step-by-step cutting and reassembly techniques and shows how to keep track of gnomonic quantities or algebraic sums of areas for subsequent constructions or comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding unknown sides of polygons/polygons built from triangles (use triangle constructions to generate polygon sides)
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating polygons (e.g., pentagon) from triangles, use the triangles' catheti and angles to determine the polygonal side lengths and internal angles: instructions scattered as 'petagono ... trova il catetto ... forma il petagono ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method: reduce the polygon construction to a triangle problem (find a particular cathetus or chord), then replicate or rotate the triangle to form the polygon; guidance includes which triangles to form and how to use existing sides as generators for polygon edges.
